key_insight: A foundation-model-based temporal scorer can pick the best ultrasound frame for optic nerve sheath diameter measurement using sparse labels and soft targets.
clinical_relevance: This could make ONSD ultrasound easier to use in low-resource settings by helping less experienced operators identify frames suitable for intracranial pressure assessment.
method: Extract per-frame embeddings from an ultrasound foundation model.
Feed embeddings into a lightweight temporal head to score each video frame.
Train with Gaussian soft labels around key frames instead of hard 0/1 labels.
evidence_signal: In subject-level cross-validation on 18 subjects and 323 videos across nine sweep types, the method selected an optimal frame in 82.2% of evaluated sweeps, outperforming the strongest training-free baseline and hard-label classification.
watch_item: Performance depends on the quality of sparse key-frame labels and still needs validation in broader, real-world ultrasound workflows before deployment.
paper_title: Soft Temporal Scoring Using a Foundation Model: Optimal Frame Selection for Improved ONSD Measurement in Ultrasound Videos
